outcome: Presence of Methanobrevibacter (M.) smithii in meconium
cohort: The study participants were 33 preterm neonates from whom meconium samples were collected.
finding: Methanogens, specifically Methanobrevibacter (M.) smithii, were widely detected in the meconium of preterm neonates, positioning them as early inhabitants of the human gut immediately after birth.
mod_finding: C-section delivery was significantly correlated with the PCR-detection of methanogens in meconium.
cross-section timing: Immediately after birth, using meconium samples.
